articles.summary: Pharmaceutical companies Moderna and Merck announced today the highly promising results of their anti-cancer mRNA vaccine Phase 3 clinical trial targeting later-stage melanoma skin cancers. Researchers sequenced the DNA from each patient's tumors to create personalized vaccines that, when injected, rev up the immune system to destroy the cancer cells while leaving healthy tissues alone. The versatile mRNA platform enables researchers to manufacture bespoke vaccines for each patient in just six weeks. Some arms of the clinical trial paired the new mRNA vaccines with Merck's Keytruda, a monoclonal antibody checkpoint inhibitor that enables immune cells to identify and kill cancer cells. The patients in the clinical trial had been diagnosed with Stage IIB to Stage IV melanoma cancers. All had visible signs of their tumors surgically removed before beginning the clinical trial. Around 112,000 Americans are diagnosed with melanoma each year, and about 8,500 die of the disease. The five-year survival rate for Stage IIB is around 87 percent , falling to 35 percent for Stage IV patients. The coupling prolonged the time before the cancer returned and reduced the chance it would spread to other organs.
